summary: Three material test-oracle defects require revision. Independent normal scoped run reproduced 44 failures and 5 passing controls; missing public auth inputs are real RED, while deeper auth/file/redaction behavior remains latent.

findings.description: The descriptor observer rejects correct bounded reads and requires particular Python read entry points, beyond the frozen opened-descriptor contract.
findings.evidence: Original lines413-414/424-425 sum requested sizes rather than bytes returned. On the real owned0600 KEY descriptor, read(4097) returns64 bytes; a bounded EOF read(4033) is rejected although total content remains64 bytes. A single validated io.FileIO(fd).read(4097) also returns64 correctly but leaves reads empty and fails line457. The same observer accepts a single os.read(4097) parent. Reproduced with original AST-extracted observers in /tmp/raw-auth-test-gate/manifests/public-and-oracle-results.json; this is oracle sensitivity, not future-client GREEN.
findings.fix: Observe actual credential bytes and validation/reopen ordering without imposing a read primitive or total requested-size sum. Retain the4097 cap and real opened-descriptor/path-replacement/closure controls; qualify the observer with a bounded short-read/EOF loop and a standard descriptor stream as valid parents.

findings.description: Five malformed-file privacy checks track KEY after replacing the file with unrelated bytes, so disclosed rejected credential content can pass.
findings.evidence: Lines332-338 use a*4097, one\ntwo, space-padded key, key\x00 and key\xff; line370 only checks KEY and the private path. Original no_leak(diagnostics(ValueError("invalid credential content: "+repr(payload))), KEY, path, basename) accepts complete payload disclosure for all five, with a generic redacted refusal as valid parent and actual KEY disclosure correctly rejected. Reproduced in public-and-oracle-results.json. An implementation that handles valid credentials privately but echoes only malformed input would escape these cases. Current parser RED does not exercise this assertion against a file loader.
findings.fix: Place an independently observable unique credential sentinel in each nonempty malformed payload and check its raw/escaped diagnostic forms, or check the actual payload. Keep each invalidity isolated, and pair the original assertion with a leaking diagnostic and a redacted valid refusal; do not replace the loader.

findings.description: Negative metadata cases observe final refusal but cannot reject reading credential content before owner/mode validation, contrary to the frozen before-content-read requirement.
findings.evidence: Lines344-361 wrap open/fstat only; lines365-373 and579-590 check typed/private refusal and absent HTTP/output, with no read observation. The valid-file descriptor case merely records fstat before reading. Consequently open(flags), fstat(fd), read(fd,4097), then reject foreign uid/insecure mode satisfies these observers and final assertions while violating the required order. Original observer-only real-FD probes allow64-byte reads on both0640 and injected foreign-owner descriptors, alongside0400/0600 valid parents; metadata-oracle-results.json records this sensitivity gap, not a future implementation run.
findings.fix: At the real CLI boundary, make attempted credential reads observable for the existing foreign-owner/insecure-mode cases and assert zero reads before their refusal, paired with runner-owned0400/0600 parents that do read and proceed. Cover supported descriptor read paths without naming a private loader or constraining stat representation/syscall choice.
